newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-Seles sues German Tennis Federation over stabbing.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-Seles sues German Tennis Federation over stabbing.

text.p: Lawyers for Monica Seles on Wednesday opened a 24.4 million mark ($16.3 million) damages suit against the German Tennis Federation for alleged failure to ensure security at an event where she was stabbed in 1993.
Seles wants compensation for lost earnings in her 27-month break from competition, and argues the Federation did not take necessary precautions to prevent the attack at the Hamburg Open.

Her lawyer Wilhelm Danelzik told the court the players' bench in the stadium was too close to the spectators' stand, from where east German lathe operator Guenter Parche leapt to stab Seles in the back with a kitchen knife.
Danelzik said worldwide standards provided for the bench to be at least three metres (yards) from spectators.
But the Federation says the safety measures at the time of the attack were sufficient and the standards were not binding.
After the stabbing the then world number one several times postponed her return to the international circuit. Her lawyer said she suffered from fear and depression.

Parche was given a two-year suspended sentence for grievous bodily harm but freed immediately by a Hamburg court in April 1995 when a judge ruled he was emotionally retarded and might not have been entirely responsible for his actions.
Seles's attorney and the Hamburg prosecutor had asked the court to jail Parche for attempted murder. A subsequent appeal by Seles for a harder sentence failed.
Parche said at the time he wanted to wound Seles out of love for her German rival, Steffi Graf.
The court will rule by December 19 at the latest.
